findings_to_judge.finding: Both of Dell's closest server-assembler comparables reported the overlapping April-June 2026 quarter in mid-August with massive margin upside in the teeth of the memory spike - Super Micro delivered 17.5% GAAP gross margin on 11 Aug against its own prior guidance of 8.2-8.4%, and Lenovo's ISG posted a record 9.1% operating margin on 13 Aug against a ~4.6% consensus - which is the direct empirical refutation of the 'the assembler eats the memory bill' thesis that Dell's own preview coverage says is the whole question for this print.

IDC's calendar-Q2 2026 PC data, covering two of the three months of Dell's fiscal Q2, shows the memory shortage working as a pricing-power event rather than a margin event for OEMs - shipments fell 4.9% to 68.2m units and Dell fell 5% to 9.3m while industry revenue rose, with comparable-line prices up 20-40% year over year and IDC stating vendors 'are pushing through price increases faster than demand is dropping'; Dell held share at 13.6%.
